AIR_2024q1.summary_analysis: AAR Corp. reported fiscal third-quarter 2024 results, and Seeking Alpha reported AAR shares were trading more than 6% lower after the report. Revenue was essentially in line with estimates and adjusted EPS narrowly beat consensus, while GAAP earnings fell sharply on acquisition-related financing and integration costs following the March 1 close of the $725 million Triumph Group Product Support acquisition.
AIR_2024q1.explicit_reasons: The articles do not explicitly attribute the stock's drop to any specific factor; Seeking Alpha reported only that shares were trading more than 6% lower after the report, alongside separate commentary on the newly closed acquisition's expected contribution.
AIR_2024q1.implicit_reasons: Revenue of $567.3 million was essentially in line with the Zacks Consensus Estimate (a roughly 0.06%-0.1% miss), up nearly 9% year over year with commercial sales up 18% and government sales down 7%, while adjusted EPS of $0.85 beat the $0.84 consensus by 1.19% even as GAAP EPS fell to $0.39 from $0.62 a year earlier. Net interest expense rose to $11.3 million from $3.5 million, including $6.1 million of bridge financing costs and $12.2 million of acquisition and amortization expenses tied to the March 1 close of the $725 million Triumph Group Product Support acquisition, and SG&A separately included $2.0 million of costs related to an investigation. Seeking Alpha noted the acquisition is expected to add 13% to sales and 38% to adjusted operating profit.

Guidance.text: Seeking Alpha reported the newly closed Triumph Group Product Support acquisition is expected to add 13% to sales and 38% to adjusted operating profit; the article gives no baseline figure to compare this against beyond describing it as the deal's expected contribution.

Revenue.text: Revenue of $567.3 million missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $567.63 million by about 0.06%-0.1%, though it was up nearly 9% from $521.1 million a year earlier, with commercial sales growing 18% and government sales falling 7%, per Seeking Alpha.

Profits, costs and margin.text: Adjusted EPS of $0.85 beat the $0.84 consensus estimate by 1.19% and was up from $0.75 a year earlier, but GAAP earnings from continuing operations fell to $0.39 per share from $0.62 a year earlier.

Debt, leverage and capital raise.text: Net interest expense rose to $11.3 million from $3.5 million a year earlier, including $6.1 million of bridge financing costs, and SG&A included $12.2 million of acquisition and amortization expenses, tied to the March 1 close of the $725 million Triumph Group Product Support acquisition, which was financed with $550 million of new senior notes and revolver borrowings under an upsized $825 million credit facility; the articles give no expectation for this.

Litigation.text: SG&A for the quarter included $2.0 million of costs related to an investigation; the articles give no further detail or expectation for this.
